sense.text:
Here is why Benjamin roll the way they roll in the islands. The brothers up here in America, their spirit is more alive than the brothers in the islands. Anywhere outside of Babylon is relaxed: tropical water, not defiled there as much as it is here, so it is a more relaxed spirit over there, and there is not really a sense of urgency, because of the weather, the temperature, the water, the food, the beach. You see birds diving in the water and coming out with fish. You are not surrounded by buildings and garbage. In the islands there was no racism to experience; you climb coconut trees, go on the beach, go fishing, just relax.

“And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the Lord”: the Lord love Benjamin; we are beloved. The Lord love all the 12 tribes, but he never said the beloved of Levi. Levi didn’t have no part of the land.

“Shall dwell in safety”: that is the reason the brothers in the islands are laid back. They didn’t grow up around the racism that you see straight forward. The brothers here in America been fighting the white man ever since they’ve been here on the shores of America; that is why it says of Judah, ‘his hand shall be in the neck of his enemy’. The American blacks is a different breed: they’ve been fighting the white men so long they understand oppression. Benjamin does not. Tell them in the islands the white man is the devil and they don’t acknowledge it the way we acknowledge it. They don’t see the force of it, but it’s there.

“Let brotherly love continue”: that is what this whole thing is all about. If we walk in that spirit of Christ we’re going to be all right; there can never be division among us. We have to speak the same thing.

The leader that is over you is to watch over you and make sure that you are exalted, and make sure they are doing what they are supposed to be doing. Bring fire to the islands; wherever you are at, follow the same thing. We have to become greater leaders, better than what we think we are.

Even the leaders in IUIC push themselves to evolve and become better leaders. Watch them from four years ago, three years ago: every last one of them is changing, so they can lead the people in righteousness and be an example.

In Syria the Arabs over there are celebrating Christmas to this day, with a Christmas tree. Not just the Arabs: everybody on the earth celebrates Christmas. Even in India they got Christmas trees, all over the world. This is in Bible prophecy.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints”: the white man made war with the Israelites, the Negroes. “And to overcome them”: he enslaved us.

“And power was given him over all kindreds”: the Chinese, the Arabs, the Japanese. Power was given the white man over all people on the earth, “and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: worship who? Him. Get the image of Santa Claus and Jesus. The Arabs are worshiping the white man; they are celebrating Christmas over there. In China they are celebrating Christmas too, and in Africa a lot of them are celebrating Christmas. They are worshiping the white image of Christ, worshiping the white man as God. They say they are celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ, but the real Christ was not born on December 25th.

“Whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world”: if your name is not written in the book, the Bible says you will worship the white man.

Santa Claus is St Nicholas. St Nicholas was a pope; he wrote the papal bulls and he enslaved the Negroes. That is one part of what Christmas is about. There was also a black St Nicholas, whitewashed, who gave gifts to children in the Dark Ages, but the Nicholas they are referencing is the one that enslaved us.

You got Israelites now trying to renege on Jeremiah 10, trying to say Jeremiah 10 is not talking about Christmas and it’s not a tree, it was an idol being woven out of the tree. When they get around that season they get desperate, they get wicked as hell. After a while a lot of Israel is going to start fading off, becoming Christians and attacking us.

“Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely”: an example of dealing falsely is teaching that the Messiah’s birth was on December 25th. That’s a false deal, that’s a lie. You have to explain in the Bible where that’s written, or where the Messiah himself was observing it, or where he gave the ordinance to observe it, or his disciples observing it. If you cannot, you’re dealing falsely.

“Neither lie one to another”: when you tell someone else he was born that day, you’re lying. Y’all think y’all slick; we see you, we hear you, and you’re the devil the Bible speaks of, the black ones.

A lot of heresies will come into Israel, and a lot of heresies are in Israel, but it’s a try. Some of y’all want to give your kids gifts on Christmas, some of y’all love that Christmas Eve, that Christmas spirit, your wife wants to celebrate it, so some of you will find teachers with itching ears, saying there’s nothing wrong with it, it has nothing to do with slavery, nothing to do with paganism, it’s just for the kids.

Because brothers and sisters all over the world are rising up and teaching that Christmas is pagan, the Christians are trying to do damage control. Now they say, don’t slander the brothers and sisters who choose to celebrate; give each other grace in the non-essentials. Correction is not slander: if somebody is evil, you are going to say that’s evil. They say that because they want to hold on to celebrating Christmas. And now you got Israel coming up saying the exact same thing. We’re in the age of information: if you’re ignorant about these holidays being pagan there’s something wrong with you; you can easily look it up and see Christmas is pagan, Easter is pagan. A lot of so-called Christians are catching on, so these Christians are starting to mobilize and adapt, saying give us grace. No, it’s pagan. They want to join both parties, the same thing they do with politics, Democrat one day, Republican the next; they want to use Christ like that.

“Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love?” These holidays have to do with families; Esau claimed those are family holidays. So these wicked Israelites, these wicked of our people, are trying to change their way to be loved, because they ain’t about the love of Christ, they’re about the love of themselves.

“Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.” God is clear, but it’s us that’s playing the simple cards, because we don’t want to apply God’s commandment. We don’t want to show no love to these commandments, so we find a way to serve the damn devil.

This is our job, the job of the sons of God, for you Christians. The same way John the Baptist told Herod that sleeping with his brother’s wife was wicked, was wrong, and he got killed for it: Herod’s wife got upset and wanted John the Baptist’s head for what he said.

“Casting down imaginations”: you Christians might imagine that Jesus Christ was born December 25th. Our job is not to agree with you or just leave you in that foolishness. Our love is to cast that imagination down. An imagination is something you are imagining that’s not real, not true, made up.

“And every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”: the knowledge of God does not say Christ was a white man, and it does not say Christ was born on December 25th. So when them lies are being taught, our job is to cast it down. It ain’t no slander. Slander is when you lie on somebody, you dumb Christians.

Back to Jeremiah 2: this is that little speech about slander, right here.

“Yet thou sayest, Because I am innocent, surely his anger shall turn from me”: we do it for family, we don’t do it because it’s pagan; we do it to get together; we’re all home from work, we got the time off, so we take this time to spend with family. It’s innocent, nothing wrong with it, it’s just a tree, what’s the big deal?

“Behold, I will plead with thee”: God said, I’m going to kill you. That is what plead means. It sounds nice, but I’m still going to kill you. “Because thou sayest, I have not sinned”: they say it’s not sin, we’re honoring the Lord; if it’s not his birthday, we’re just giving honor to his birth.

“Why gaddest thou about so much to change thy way?” To gad is to talk too much, to give excuses. God’s way is one way. You say, no, I’mma talk my way out of this way, I’mma talk my way into that direction over there, what I want to do.

“Thou also shalt be ashamed of Egypt”: Egypt is here; America is Egypt now. When Christ returns you’re going to be ashamed of that, “as thou wast ashamed of Assyria”: ashamed of your captivity, for making excuses for celebrating those customs of Egypt and Assyria, and now America, Babylon, the same thing. It’s the same mindset as those who worship on a Sunday and say there’s nothing wrong with that. You’re going to get killed for that.

This is the simple logic right here; this is what our God told us. “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”: the Lord is the one speaking here, and he is speaking to the house of Israel.

“Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen.” This scripture is a default for everything. If you don’t understand whether what you’re doing is wrong or right, pagan or not, go into the scriptures: if it’s not a custom of the Israelites, and it’s not in the Bible where God said to do it, you have learned the ways of the heathen. That is a simple principle we all should live by, and it will keep you from getting caught up in foolishness and pagan customs.

Anything the white man does, none of us should be doing it: their ways, their customs, none of them things we should follow. We got our own customs in the Bible, the laws, the holy days. You want a holiday? That’s what holiday means: holy day. What’s holy about Christmas? Ask yourself that. God gave us holy days to keep.

“For the customs of the people are vain”: the customs they follow, their traditions, their holidays, it’s lies. That’s what vain means.

“For one cutteth a tree out of the forest”: this is literally an ancient Babylonian holiday, and America has adopted it. That is what you see taking place today. That’s how simple it is.

These Christians are getting mad because the brothers and sisters teaching what this Bible says are opening the people’s eyes. Millions of our people all over the world don’t celebrate Christmas no more; they understand Christmas is pagan. So the Christians are trying to do damage control.

“When I remember these things, I pour out my soul in me: for I had gone with the multitude”. David says he went, not just him alone, but with the multitude of people, the righteous. “I went with them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, with a multitude that kept holyday.” A multitude that did what? That kept holy days.

So what holy days did David keep? Was it Christmas? Was it Thanksgiving? Was it New Year’s? The days that David kept as holy, his holidays, are found in the Bible. That’s just clear cut. You want to find the word holiday in the Bible, that’s it right there, spelled h-o-l-y-d-a-y, with a y instead of an i. Holiday and holy day are the same exact word.

That scripture is bad. Y’all pull that one from now on: what holy days did David keep?

They’re going to run to this one, so we beat you to it before you run there. “Let no man therefore judge you”: stop. They go, see, let no man therefore judge you, only God can judge, thus saith Tupac. “In meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday”: the holy day here is the same holy day that David referred to. They say, so no one can judge you based on the holidays you keep. Oh, that’s what that means? You can’t judge me for the holidays that I keep? That’s deep.

But stop at “or in drink”. What drink? Don’t judge you for drinking water? For drinking piss, for drinking vomit? Is it alkaline water, tap water, soda, battery fluid, fuel, hot boiling water? They’ll say meat means shrimp, catfish, clam: all right, cool, I can’t judge you for eating that stuff. Then what’s the drink part? They never answer it; they’re stumped, they don’t know what it’s talking about. If you can’t explain the drink, you can’t explain holy day either, so you’re wrong on both accounts. That’s how you deal with people in Christianity and the cults.

Hold the whole verse: meat, drink, “an holyday”, “the new moon”, “the sabbath days.” He’s not talking about Thanksgiving, New Year’s, Christmas or Halloween.

precepts.why:
Here is what he is referring to. “And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings”: let no man judge you in meat offerings. “And drink offerings”: judge you in drink offerings. “In the feasts”: the feast days, the solemn days, the holy days. “And in the new moons”: the new moons are in Colossians 2:16. “And in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.”

So no man was to judge you based upon the sacrifices, the meat or drink offerings, or the ones that pertain to the sabbath days, feast days or new moons, because those pertain to Temple law. Christ died; the sacrifice is done away with. That’s what Colossians is talking about, so don’t let them Christians pull that on you.

sense.text:
When was Christ born? Not the month you would give for your own birthday. Christ was born during Passover, on the fifteenth day of the first month, the month of Abib. Don’t say April or March, because Passover usually falls late March, early April; say the fifteenth of the first month.

Christ was born under the Passover, and guess what, he died under the Passover. Christ is that Passover sacrifice, that lamb. “Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.” They go to Jerusalem every year, at the feast of the Passover. “And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem”. Christ was born in the Passover and he died on the Passover.

“And she brought forth her firstborn son”: Mary brought forth her firstborn son. Firstborn meaning Mary had other kids; it wasn’t just Christ alone. “And wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.” The inn is the hotels.

Why wasn’t there no room in the inn? Because it was Passover, the time all the men had to come up for that feast, so it was a very busy time. Everybody had to come up to Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover, so if you ain’t book your room in advance, you couldn’t get one. It’s like when they got these Super Bowls and big events in certain cities: you try to book a hotel room and you can’t find no room, because everybody is there. It was the same thing at that time, when Mary was giving birth to Christ around the Passover.
“And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.”

“And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.” You got shepherds with the animals outside, at night time. In winter time you don’t have your animals out in the field in the cold winter night; that makes no sense, especially December 25th. It’s brick outside, it’s freezing. There’s no way you got your flock out at night in the field at that time.

precepts.why:
Winter is called in the Bible ‘the mean season’. Read this: a valiant man “who had done many acts, he slew two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow”. In time of what? In time of snow. It snowed in that part of the world.

So hold that when you go back to Luke 2: if there was a time of snow, the shepherds would not be abiding in the field keeping watch over their flock by night in the dead of winter.

sense.text:
Where was Christ born? In Bethlehem, the city of David. But which part of Bethlehem did she give birth in? Was it a manger? That’s what Christianity teaches us: that the baby was born in a manger, in a barn with animals. No. We about to mess these Christians up.

“Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth”. There thy mother what? There thy mother brought thee forth. Christ was born under an apple tree. After he was born under the apple tree, he was put in the manger, because there was no room in the inn.

Imagine what Mary was going through. Sometimes sisters go through things in pregnancy and they’re like, Lord, if I’m going through all of this, I thought I was blessed. Joseph and Mary went up to Jerusalem; it was the Passover; they were trying to get a room and couldn’t find one; she was trying to find some place to stay and they ain’t got nowhere to stay. Guess what: the water bag burst, the baby came down, and she gave birth to Christ outside, under an apple tree. Then she wrapped him in a cloth and put him in the manger. Under an apple tree, not in the snow. And when do the apples be? In the springtime, not in the dead of winter.

That’s why precept upon precept is very important. Everything you learn in Christianity is a lie.

Another Christmas precept. “And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry”: Merry Christmas. “And shall send gifts one to another”: that’s where they start sending gifts one to another; that’s what Santa Claus is about, Saint Nicholas. They instituted slavery and enslaved us in Spain; that’s what this is going into. “Because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth.”

The two prophets is talking twofold. First and foremost it’s going into Elijah and Moses. Elijah used to make mockery of the heathens and killed them; Elijah called on fire from heaven and killed a lot of people one time. And Moses: the Lord was dealing with Moses at the Red Sea and drowned all the Egyptians. So the two prophets are them two witnesses.

But it’s also going into Israel, the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom, and into the twelve tribes of Israel, because the Most High God called Israel his witnesses. So first and foremost it is them two witnesses, them two prophets, but it is also going into us. Now here is what it means that we tormented them.

precepts.why:
What David used to do to this nation. “And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it. And he took their king’s crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David’s head.” He took the crown off the king and put it on his own head, disrespecting him. “And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance”: he took all their wealth.

“And he brought forth the people that were therein”, the people that king once ruled over, “and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln”. The brickkiln is an oven: David put them in ovens. You might think he made them work under saws and with axes; read on and see what that means. “And thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon”: not just one city, many cities. “So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.”

This shows what ‘under saws’ means. “And it came to pass, that after the year was expired, at the time that kings go out to battle, Joab led forth the power of the army, and wasted the country of the children of Ammon”: he wasted it. “And came and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried at Jerusalem. And Joab smote Rabbah, and destroyed it.” David let Joab have fun: you go conquer them, I’ll come after you finish.

“And David took the crown of their king from off his head, and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it”: this is heavy, I like this crown, put it on my own head. “And it was set upon David’s head: and he brought also exceeding much spoil out of the city.”

“And he brought out the people that were in it”, the Ammonites, “and cut them with saws”: there we go. Cut them with saws, “and with harrows of iron”, knives and blades, “and with axes.” David took his time; he made the king watch. David was methodically vicious to the heathen. “Even so dealt David with all the cities of the children of Ammon”, including putting them in the ovens, the brickkiln that’s left out here. “And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem”: he went home and relaxed.

That’s what David did. That goes back to the two prophets tormenting the nations, terrible things.

sense.text:
We’re staying in the same chapter. In the past we tormented them, but here is also what it’s going into. Remember these two olive trees, these two witnesses, are going into first them two prophets, and also into the nation of Israel, those two kingdoms.

“And I will give power unto my two witnesses”: God says he’s going to give power unto them two witnesses. “And they shall prophesy”: that power is the Holy Spirit, and they’re going to prophesy. That power is the Holy Spirit entering into us, and us prophesying, “a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth.”
“These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth.”

“And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies”. That’s some good stuff right there. If any man hurt them, fire goes and proceeds out of their mouth and destroys their enemies. “And if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed”: by this manner he’s got to be killed. How? Fire is going to come out of their mouth and consume them.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Because ye speak this word”: because we speak this word. “Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire”: God’s word in our mouth is like fire. “And this people wood”: the nations are going to be wood.

So everybody that hurts the sons of God, the prophets of God, fire is going to come out of their mouth, and by that fire they’re going to die. That fire goes back to us teaching God’s judgment, teaching thus saith the Lord. When the witnesses and the prophets teach the word of God, which is the fire, they are marking people for dead. Remember Christ said that anybody that don’t want to hear you, dust off your feet; it’s going to be more tolerable for them that were in the land of Sodom and Gomorrah than for them. That’s the fire destroying them, because what destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah? Fire.

In this manner shall they be killed. When it says these prophets tormented them that dwell on the earth, how do we terrorize the nations? “And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt”: we are going to be a terror unto Egypt, and Egypt here is America. Remember what we just read: they that dwell upon the earth rejoice and make merry and send gifts one to another, because these two prophets tormented them.

That’s the sons of God, the witnesses, rising up here in America and teaching. When you teach the word of God, you are going to be a terror unto this place, because what you teach is going to come to pass; you are proclaiming judgment on Babylon. “Every one that maketh mention thereof shall be afraid in himself”: they’re going to be afraid of the word of God, of what we are teaching, “because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he hath determined against it.” And what is the counsel of the Lord of hosts? That this place is going to be burnt with fire. Any man hurt these two witnesses, thus shall they be killed.

“And then shall that Wicked be revealed”: that’s the white man, those that are going to hurt us here in America, the Caucasian race. “Whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth”: how would the Lord consume the wicked with the spirit of his mouth? First and foremost it starts off with us teaching the word of God, condemning them and marking them for death, because the Most High God’s word is literally like fire. “And shall destroy with the brightness of his coming”: when he returns he’s going to destroy them.

Here is the Lord consuming them with the spirit of his mouth. “And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest; And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame”. Who is going to do this? Christ. It’s like unto a flame. “And he shall destroy them without labour by the law”.

So Christ is just going to open his mouth, and the law of God is going to come out of his mouth, which is fire, and he’s going to destroy the nations. He just opens his mouth speaking God’s laws, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not commit adultery, and his fire comes out of his mouth burning up all the wicked. That goes back to whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.

sense.text:
Read it one more time. “And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them”. We torment them with the word of God. We tormented them by prophesying and teaching thus saith the Lord.

Remember the Lord sending plagues. Why is God sending plagues on the earth? It says these two prophets tormented them. You’re going to learn today why God is sending plagues, and how God’s plagues come upon the earth.

precepts.why:

But what is the process for the Lord doing it? “Surely the Lord God will do nothing”: the Lord is not going to do nothing, he ain’t bringing evil on a city, “but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” He reveals what he’s going to do, the secrets in the Bible, to his servants the prophets.

“The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord God hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” What are we going to do? Prophesy. Remember in Revelation he gave these prophets power and they prophesied. When they prophesy, evil is going to take place in a city. All of that goes back to fire coming forth from their mouth; all of that goes back to they tormented them that dwell on the earth.

We torment them when we teach the word of God: plagues come forth on the earth. We got that power. You brothers got that power inside of you. When you teach, you bring plagues on the earth. The Lord is not doing nothing until he reveals his secrets to you and you teach it, and as you teach it he does the things that you say are going to happen.

“Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt”: Egypt here is America. God is letting us know who to prophesy against.

sense.text:
A brother asked about the history of the 1611 King James Bible and King James. King James was not a homosexual. He was slandered by two men, Anthony Weldon and Francis Osborne, who put that rumor out 25 years after he died, and they hated him because he fired them from Parliament. He had a wife and about eight or nine children, and he was one of the most revered and highly regarded kings of his time; many of his contemporaries said it was a lie and a slander. That lie was buried, and then the homosexuals came up, found it and resurrected it.

“The law of the Lord is perfect.” A lot of people try to say the white man wrote the Bible, King James was a white man and he wrote the Bible. But when you go into the Bible you find laws, statutes and commandments, and the Bible lets us know what is going to happen in the future; you could go into the Bible and show what is going on in Syria right now. The Bible is made up of laws for the children of Israel.

“Converting the soul”: it teaches you how to change.

“The Lord gave the word.” When you read the Bible you read about Jeremiah, Isaiah, Daniel, Ezra, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John: the Lord gave the word to all these men.

“Great was the company of those that published it”: the men that published it are the men that wrote the Bible. They were great men; they were prophets. Not King James.

A lot of the time they say King James wrote the Bible. King James did not write the Bible. When Elizabeth died in 1603 the crown passed to James, who had been King of Scotland, and several months after he ascended the throne of England he authorized a new translation of the Bible. Authorized: all he did was authorize the Bible to be translated from Greek, Hebrew and Latin into English. He did not sit down and write it, and to prove that, there are older manuscripts you can go and look at and you will see the same thing that is in the 1611.

It was to replace the Bishops’ Bible, because that Bible spoke evil against the king being king over the land, and there were traditions written within it, so he wanted it removed. There were many Bibles before the King James Version, and by scholarly sources it is by far the best translation of all the translations before it. That is why it says in the Bible itself, ‘translated out of the original tongues and with former translations diligently compared and revised by his Majesty’s special command’: by his command, not his hand, as if he wrote it. He hired the best: men who spoke the languages and were well versed in the versions before it, who took from those versions and made it better. There were actually 52 of them, but some dropped out and 47 remained.

Those 47 of the best Hebrew and Greek scholars of the day were divided into six groups: three for the Old Testament, two for the New, and one for the Apocrypha. That is why the Apocrypha is part of the Bible. Two of the groups met at Oxford, two at Cambridge and two at Westminster. When a group completed its task, its work went to twelve men, two from each panel; final differences were settled at a general meeting, and in special difficulty learned men outside were consulted, to make sure the translation was right. Translation, not interpretation: changing it from one language to another language, correct the best they could.

King James is behind a great work. It is the best-selling, thousands of people learned the word of God from that translation alone, and it is the top tier of all translations. That is why all the versions that came after it, the New International, the New King James Version, the ESV, are revised versions of that one.

I am going to show you God was behind that translation. “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death”: the valley of the shadow of death is America, the land of your captivity. “I will fear no evil: for thou art with me”: God is with us. “Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”

“Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.” What is that table? The table is the Bible. The Most High is such a mastermind: the white man read the Bible and said, I am going to teach them their own book. The Most High made it so the white man did not change the Bible and did not burn the Bible.

So when it says he prepareth a table before me in the presence of our enemies, which is the so-called white man, it is saying God was behind the Bible being translated and the gathering of the books. Our enemies did not write this book; God prepared this book for us today. When King James had the Hebrew scholars and the brothers that spoke Greek put it together, the Lord was there guiding, making sure it was prepared for us, and he made sure they did not burn or destroy the Bible. Why? Because the prophecy is that after 350 years the spirit of life from God is going to enter into us, we will stand up on our feet, and great fear is going to fall upon them that see us. The prophecy is that we are going to wake up to the truth that we are the Israelites, and we wake up through the Bible.

You could get the Bible anywhere, but the white men were so prideful they said we would never understand this book was talking about us.
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures.”

“He restoreth my soul.” To restore your soul is to bring back to remembrance who you are. Without the Bible we would not have known that we are the children of Israel, because all the history books about us have been hidden. God prepared this book for us in the presence of our enemy, and the Lord God says, he restoreth my soul. King James putting the Bible together, the Most High God was behind all of that.

The scripture read earlier: “great was the company”. A lot of brothers will question the Bible, but we bring in precept to back up what the scriptures say: precept must be upon precept.

“The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.” That is what we just read about King James. Men don’t believe God is in power of everything. When you deny the power of God, you deny yourself.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. When the Bible was written by the prophets it was written pretty much entirely in Hebrew and Aramaic, in letters and scrolls. In the midst of those letters and scrolls you can put the pieces together: the Most High gave this prophet this part of the puzzle, that prophet that part of the puzzle, in the language they spoke at the time. Then the Lord moved the spirit for this to happen.

“For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.” Another tongue, another language: that goes back to the Bible being translated out of one language into another. That’s prophetic.

Remember a man named William Tyndale. When England was run by the Catholic church the Bible was written in Latin, and it was illegal for the people to read it on their own; they had to go to the church and hear it translated to them out of the Catholic priest’s mouth. Tyndale said this is not fair, it should be for public use. He was the first to set forth putting it in English, and he was killed for doing it. Most of the King James Version Bible comes primarily from his work into English, and that is how it started.

precepts.why:
“In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people”. Paul is calling Isaiah’s word the law too. Paul spoke Greek, he spoke Latin, and surely Hebrew as well, so Paul spoke the words of God in a multitude of languages; and when you read Acts 2, the disciples were given the spirit to speak the word of God in multiple languages.

Watch this: “and yet for all that”, even with it being in English and Spanish and Creole, “will they not hear me, saith the Lord.” They are still going to hate it and still go against God’s word, regardless of what language it is written in.

So don’t let nothing shake your faith concerning the word of God. This book is a true book. Where else can you read about us going into slavery thousands of years before it happened? You think King James could make that up?

sense.text: “And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas”: Eli’s sons. “In one day they shall die both of them.”

“And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.” It sounds like it might be talking about Christ, but in this particular context it is referring to Samuel: the faithful priest is Samuel. It is prophetic also, Samuel but also other things in another time.

precepts.why:
Chapter 3 explains it: “And the child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision”. The faithful priest raised up after Eli’s house is Samuel.

A lot of the time, all you have to do is read the verses above it or under it, and it is going to explain what it is talking about, unless it is something prophetic. Read above the verse or under the verse to understand the context.

sense.text:
“And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.” A sister asked whether it was Christ talking with Adam in the garden or the Father; that will be gone into later.

A lot of the time, when you hear thus saith the Lord, it is the angel speaking on behalf of the Father, or Christ speaking on behalf of the Father. When you read thus saith the Lord God, it is not God speaking. The word angel means messenger: they bring the message, and whose message do they bring? God’s message. So when people hear that voice they say, that’s God speaking; no, it’s the angels, or it might be Christ. It sounds like it’s God, but it’s the angel.

That verse gives us a lot of understanding of who we were dealing with and who we are dealing with now. Nobody ever heard God’s voice; and when we say God here, we mean the Father himself, our grandfather, Christ’s Father.

That’s a good chapter right there, and a good verse too. “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” A brother asked whether that sacrifice could also be the sacrifice of Romans 12, since the chapter speaks of Christ coming to gather us. Yes, you can use that scripture in Romans 12: the sacrifice is making yourself a living sacrifice, ready to die for this.

precepts.why:
“I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Remember what Christ said: he that saveth his life shall lose his life. You have to be ready; you have to become a living sacrifice.

It does not just mean you give up certain things in this world. It literally means you have to be willing to die for what you believe in, willing to die for your king. If you are ready to make that sacrifice, take your cross and follow after Christ.

A lot of the time people don’t understand: proclaiming Christ, the things you teach could get you killed. You think the white man enslaved us and hid this truth from us for hundreds of years for you negro to just come and take the Bible and start teaching truth back on the earth? No, he will kill us. He is going to kill a lot of the leaders.

This proves it. “And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain”: that is sacrifice, they were slain, “for the word of God”. Why does it say the altar? Because they were sacrifices: that is them making themselves a living sacrifice.

They were killed for the word of God because they were teaching the word of God. They were teaching Christ, and they were killed for it. So becoming a living sacrifice means you don’t just change your life and give up certain things in this world; you literally become a sacrifice. Once you are a soldier and you go to war, know that there are casualties.

sense.text: A brother asked, since John called the angel his brethren, does that mean we are angels in bodily form, that we were once angels? “But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage”.

“Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels”. We are equal unto the angels. Not like equal; if you are equal to an angel, what does that make you? You are an angel.

Before Christ came on this earth in the flesh he had a body in the heavens; he was in his eternal form. It is the same thing with us. The angels are our brothers, our heavenly siblings: when you die you go to your people, and if you are righteous you go back to Christ, and the angels are our people.

precepts.why:
How do we become equal to an angel again? “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved”: this body is destroyed. “We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” It says we have an eternal body in the heavens. That means we might just be in avatar state right now, and our real body is up there.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”: our body which is from heaven, that angelic body.

“If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked”: right now in this flesh we are naked; this flesh is weak. “For we that are in this tabernacle do groan”: we groan because this body is weak. “Being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon”: we want to be clothed upon, “that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” That is the angelic body.
Listen to what the angel said. “And the angel that was sent unto me, whose name was Uriel, gave me an answer”.

“Then the angel said unto me”, which angel? Uriel, “Go thy way, and tell my people what manner of things, and how great wonders of the Lord thy God, thou hast seen.” We are the same; we are brothers. We are just family, heavenly family and earthly family.

sense.text:
A brother came to this truth, came to the knowledge that he is Israel, and his wife was very resistant: drama in the house, the kids learning while she cooking on the Sabbath, and now it’s court, lawyers and alimony. He’s not alone. Hundreds of brothers, probably thousands of brothers and sisters around the world, are going through that same thing right now: they came to this knowledge, they’re trying to serve God, and their spouse don’t want to serve God.

“Think not that I am come to send peace on earth”: Christ said that. Some of you all might be married and you want a peaceful marriage, you want everything to be perfect. Guess what, Christ ain’t come to send peace on the earth: “I came not to send peace, but a sword.”

“For I am come to set a man at variance against his father”: some of your fathers is against you because of this truth. “And the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.”

“And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.” A lot of times when you come to this truth and you teach it, your enemies first and foremost start in your house: either your wife don’t believe, either your kids don’t believe, either your husband don’t believe, or your mother-in-law staying by and she don’t believe. Always remember that.

Hundreds of brothers went through exactly this. Even brothers in top leadership go through the same things you go through. The key thing is applying what the scripture says concerning it.

God hate divorce. Some of you all might hear a brother say he going through a divorce, but God hate divorce, and us here in IUIC, because God hate it, we hate it. Still, this is what the scripture says concerning the situation of a brother whose spouse won’t serve God: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases”: the bondage of marriage.

It was never set up for you to marry somebody then divorce them. From the beginning it was not so. There was no multiple wives or none of that stuff in the beginning: God created one man for one woman. That’s what it mean. You couldn’t just get rid of your woman because she ain’t right or she acting up, because she came from you; that was yours.

“But God hath called us to peace.” God call us to peace, to serve him in peace, not to be home arguing and fighting with our spouse about his laws all the time.

precepts.why:
Jump up to verse 12, to “pleased to dwell”: “But to the rest speak I, not the Lord”, if any man have “a wife that believeth not, and she be pleased to dwell”, “let him not put her away.” She don’t believe, but she’s not cooking on the Sabbath; she’s doing what God say, what you tell her to do. Why? Because she love you. She say, this is a good man, he took care of me my whole life, we got kids together, I want to keep the family together, I love this man; I don’t believe what he believe, but I’m going to do it because I love him.

So for all you brothers and sisters married to a spouse that departs: that shows that person don’t really love you. If she could go and say, I’m leaving you, I’m going to go get some new penis, I’m going to go get another man, I’m going to start over, she never loved you. A woman that really love you can’t start over. Some women can’t sleep when you not home; that’s when a woman’s desire is unto you, she keep trying to please you. But if it’s easy for her to leave and talk about divorce, she don’t really love you. Same thing with a brother: if a brother is up to leave you, sister, and he talking about divorce, that person never really did love you, don’t really care about you.

But that’s what Christ said he came to do: to send a sword, and a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

sense.text:
In this walk you’re going to see brothers lose things. Some of us is going to lose things we think we care about, things we think love us, but sometimes that’s the Most High doing us a favor.

“Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?” In this truth, brothers, you got to be willing to forsake all to follow after Christ. You going to have to give some things up; that’s how it going to go for all of us. Peter wanted to know what he going to have, because he forsook all to follow after Christ; Peter had a business.

“And every one that hath forsaken houses”: in the divorce, a lot of times, guess who they give the house to? The woman. That house was half a million dollars; in New York and these places houses is millions of dollars. You work 40 years, you retire, you paid off that house, and the government said no, give her the house because she a woman. That’s how it’s set up. So you lost your house. Brothers, you got to be willing to give up that house, man. To hell with that damn house, she could keep it. There’s nothing better than a peace of mind; you want a good peace of mind, some things you’re going to have to let go.

Or brethren, or sister, “or father, or mother, or wife, or children”. What is Christ saying here? Sometimes you might have to forsake your kids. That sound like some evil stuff, and people be talking crap about us, but Christ said it: sometimes it might reach the point where your wife leave and take them kids, and you might have to forsake them. You love your kids, but the way you got to look at it, and it’s hard, is like casualties of war. It hurt when brothers lose their kids, when the wife leave with the kids; brothers that was close to me went through that and it hurt. But we got to man up and deal with it. That’s what the Lord said is going to happen: a lot of us is going to lose things.

“Or lands, for my name’s sake”: you might got to leave the country you were born in, the country you grew up in, the land you own, the houses you own.

“Shall receive an hundredfold”: you’re going to have a hundredfold. “And shall inherit everlasting life”: you going to live forever. So when you lose these things don’t be scared, don’t worry. Just know the price is that you’re going to live forever and you going to have a hundredfold, and immortal life.

precepts.why:
What’s so heavy when brothers go through that: a lot of times we caught up in the two worlds. Understand who these kids belong to, and then you going to understand life a little bit better. “Behold, all souls are mine”: God say all souls is his. “As the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine”.

So don’t get caught up in a world where you let somebody oppress you because of your son and your daughter. Every son in this earth, every soul, belong to the Most High God. You can only do your best. Sometimes it’s going to be hard and you’re going to have to turn around, but you got to make a decision down the line.

For the brothers that got an unbelieving wife: “I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman.” To keep house means to live with. Brothers, all women is not righteous; some women is wicked as hell. The Lord said it’s better to dwell with a dragon and a lion than with a wicked woman.

While you sleeping she outside in the car getting smashed by another dude. She putting rat poison inside your food little by little, trying to take you out, because you told her you got a $5 million life insurance. She watching you like dollar signs: I’m going to kill this right here, I want to be rich. And when they leave they use the system to destroy you: they put you on child support, spousal abuse, and they say I’m going to hurt you and I’m going to destroy you. That’s what they do.

But you got to be willing to lose it for the Lord. Welcome to the club.

sense.text:
A question on how David treated the people he dealt with in 2 Samuel 12: would that be because of 2 Samuel 10:4? “Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.”

Yeah: they disrespected David, so David dealt with them. David sent to them to tell them everything is good with the new king, and they disrespected him, so David went and taught them a lesson.

A lot of you single people think that when you get married everything going to be perfect. Marriage is just the beginning; it’s trials. A brother married 12 years gets on his wife’s nerves and she gets on his, they go through arguments, and he still loves her.

“Husbands, love your wives”: all you married brothers say you love your wife. “And be not bitter against them.” Satan is like a roaring lion, and it’s easy for Satan to get involved in your relationship. A lot of times brothers become bitter towards their wife; I see that happen over and over and over. But the Bible says you must love your wife, and be not bitter against them.

Why could a man become bitter against his wife? When she call you out of your name: you can’t do nothing for me, the stuff a real typical black woman would say. If a woman calling you an ass, a punk, this and that, do she love you? No. That right there is disrespect. And if you brothers allow your woman to talk to you a certain way and you don’t correct it, something wrong with you. My wife would never call me out of my name, because there will be a serious sit down. And that does not mean abuse or hitting or none of that crap.

Keep it real: one of the main reasons all of us men become bitter towards our wife is because she not giving up the cheeks. You come home horny, you want some, and she here cleaning, washing, doing laundry, and then you fall asleep, and you get up in the morning looking at her like, I wanted some last night. Now you mad all day: don’t talk to me, man. All you brothers know that, all you sisters know that. Us men, when we want it, we want it: it’s lunch. It’s like getting between a lion and his lunch; the lion will be angry.

How you deal with a disrespectful woman? Do you slap her in the face, like woman who the hell you talking to? No, you don’t. A man that got to use physical violence for his woman to listen to him is a weak man. You deal with it according to the scriptures. You let her know, listen, I’m mad. And if that woman loves you, if she disrespect you or call you out your name, first and foremost she got to take accountability and apologize. Until you apologize, don’t cook for me, I ain’t want none of that: acknowledge what you did wrong first.

That’s why it says this in Corinthians, about the main reason a man become bitter against his wife. “Defraud ye not one the other”: fraudulent activity. “Except it be with consent”: you got to ask; it got to be with consent. Sometimes she might not be feeling well, and if a sister truly is not feeling well, brothers understand that. But some sisters fake it, and that’s evil.

“For a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency.” How can Satan tempt you? Now you become bitter, you ain’t getting none, and now you on the job looking at another woman. Or the sister on the job looking at another man, because, brother, you ain’t doing what you’re supposed to do as a husband.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things. And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth, and with labour do we find the things that are before us”. Read it again: hardly do we guess aright about the things that are upon the earth. “But the things that are in heaven who hath searched out?”

“And thy counsel who hath known”: who knows what God’s counsel is? The only way you’re going to know God’s counsel is “except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above”. Unless God give wisdom. God sends his Holy Spirit from above to come and dwell in you; that’s how he gives you wisdom. So if God’s spirit, the Holy Spirit, is not dwelling in you, that means you don’t got wisdom.

God has to send wisdom from above, the Holy Spirit from above. That’s how he makes you know the things he makes known, his counsel, the things in heaven: he’s got to send his spirit and show it to you.

“For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed”: that’s how we’re going to be reformed, meaning changed. God has got to send his Holy Spirit upon us. Brothers, do y’all got the Holy Spirit? That’s what I want to hear.

There are levels to the Holy Spirit: law, understanding, spirit and power. Once you all are in here you got the Holy Spirit on you; now whether or not it’s going to stay with you, that’s dependent on you.

precepts.why:
How you get the Holy Spirit. Christ said, “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Everybody say they love Christ, but they don’t want to keep the commandments.

“And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth”: so the Comforter is also called the Spirit of truth, “whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.” Christ is talking about himself, his Spirit dwelling in us. That’s the Holy Spirit.

“I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you. Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more”.

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name”. We read in Wisdom of Solomon that wisdom is going to come from above; that’s how you’re going to understand the things in the heavens. The Most High has got to send wisdom from above.

“He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. The Holy Spirit, the spirit of God that comes and dwells in us, teaches us. We could bring out certain scriptures and show them to you all, but unless the spirit of God opens your understanding and shows it, you’re not going to understand what we’re saying, and you ain’t going to understand what the scripture is saying. That’s just what it is.

sense.text:
Remember what we read early on: who may know what’s in the heavens, and who may know God’s counsel, except he send his Holy Spirit and show it to you.

“Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son’s name”. This is talking about somebody and their son. “If thou canst tell”: if you can tell. That’s important, because a lot of you all think you all could tell, but you can’t. You don’t know what his name is. You think you know what his name is, but you don’t. Brothers are running around talking about they got the name of the son and the father. This is Proverbs; this is Solomon writing, and at that time we were using the term yahwah. So something very heavy is being said here: you don’t know what you think you know.

Who hath ascended and descended? It’s talking about Christ.

Read it again: we know who ascended and descended, Christ. And we don’t know his name. Nobody knows his name. His son’s name, or the title we call him, is the Word of God: that’s the name when he’s in his celestial form. When he came on the earth, he came as Solomon; when he came on the earth he came as Jesus, or yahawashi, because that’s how you say Jesus in that form of Hebrew. Some people even say Yeshua. But it all means he saves; that’s what the name means.

precepts.why:
Who hath ascended and descended. “If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things? And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven”. Who is speaking here? Christ. Christ came down from heaven, “even the Son of man”, the Son of God, “which is in heaven.” He came down from heaven and he went back into heaven.

So who hath descended and ascended is letting us know it’s talking about Christ. In order to do that you’re not a regular human being. Christ is not regular: Christ is a divine power. A lot of times people downplay the power that Christ has, like he just came as a man and died. Christ created this whole planet Earth. Christ created the universe. Everything you can think of that exists, Christ created it. That makes him a God.

“And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am the Lord: And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty”. Remember: what is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou canst tell. The Lord appeared unto our forefathers by the name God Almighty.

“But by my name Jehovah”, yahawah, “was I not known to them.” So you’re telling me Abraham, Isaac and Jacob didn’t know the name? Did the Most High do a name change? What’s going on here is that it’s titles. The Lord was always using titles. Everything he gives us is titles for us to use to call him, until the kingdom is set up, because he can’t give us his true name with us being in this flesh.

Even with all the titles he’s given us, his name holds so much power that he has to give you titles. God’s name is so powerful he’s like, I got to give you titles: call me I am.

“After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven”. Christ is telling us how to deal with his father, how to pray: when we pray we’ve got to call him Father.

“Hallowed be thy name.” God’s name is hallowed, is holy. You cannot just call on God’s name, neither do you know his name. That’s why the scripture says, what is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou canst tell.

We know his son’s name when his son came on the earth: his name was Jesus, meaning he saves. Joshua is the same thing; Yeshua, yahawashi. The key thing is his name was he saves, and there were many people that came on the earth named Joshua. The same name Joshua you read in the Book of Judges, that’s Jesus’ name too; it’s the same thing.

God did not give us his holy name. Look at what we were doing when we were in the land, even till this day, and all the wickedness going on on the earth: you think God is going to give us his real true name? That’s why he says he’s going to give us his name in the kingdom, if we overcome.

“Accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.” The Bible says don’t be accustomed to swearing and to naming the Holy One, meaning you keep calling, you keep using God’s name. Even with the name, the title he gives us, don’t accustom yourself to just using it.

“For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark: so he that sweareth and nameth God continually shall not be faultless.” You’re not going to be faultless. You’re not supposed to be using God’s name like that. That’s why scripture says, Our Father which art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.

God’s name is holy, and even the title he tells us to call him by is holy. The title is like a shadow, to bring us on to the real thing, his real name. The same way you’ve got to treat his real name, treat the name he gave you, yahwah, that way too. It’s like training day.

“And this was an occasion to deceive the world: for men, serving either calamity or tyranny, did ascribe unto stones and stocks the incommunicable name.” What is the incommunicable name? Incommunicable means ‘not able to be communicated to others.’

You’re not supposed to be speaking the name of God. The only time you’re supposed to use God’s name is when you’re praying; it’s between you and him. You’re not supposed to just be talking, speaking God’s name like you see Negroes doing today. Even Amalek don’t call God by his name: they say Hashem, meaning the name. So we’re not supposed to just be naming God, calling God by his name.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS”. That’s the name he had when he came on the earth: Jesus was one of his names, his earthly name. Another one of his earthly names is Solomon. Solomon was that eternal spirit; Solomon was that God that we read about in the Bible.

“For he shall save his people from their sins.”

“And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.”

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” The Word of God is a heavenly name that they call him; that’s the name he’s called when he’s in his celestial body. But even in him being called the Word of God, there’s another name written that no man knows but he himself, and it’s not the Word of God. The Word of God is just another title for us to call him.

Who is the Word of God? Christ is the Word of God; that’s his heavenly name, the name he’s got in the heavens. “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God”. We just read that his name was called The Word of God, so this is the Word of God, that eternal spirit, in the beginning.

The God he was with is the one Proverbs speaks of: what is his name, and what is his son’s name. That’s his father.

“And the Word was God.” So what is this saying about Christ? Christ is a God. Christ is a power; he’s that eternal power. He’s a God.

sense.text: “I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions.” Who is the wisdom here talking about? The Word of God.

“The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way”. Remember we read early on, in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God. So who is the wisdom that was possessed in the beginning with the Father? It’s talking about Christ, that eternal spirit. “Before his works of old”: before he created the earth and all of that, he created, guess who, Christ.

“I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.” Before the earth was, he was set up. “When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world. When he prepared the heavens, I was there”.

“Then I was by him, as one brought up with him”: it says as one brought up with him because it’s talking about the Son of God. “And I was daily his delight”, meaning Christ was daily the delight of his father, “rejoicing always before him; Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth”.

precepts.why: “Wisdom hath been created before all things”. Before everything that you all see on the earth here was created, wisdom was created. Who is this wisdom talking about? The Word of God, the anointed. He was the first thing created: wisdom. “And the understanding of prudence from everlasting.”

“Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people. In the congregation of the most High shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power.”

“I came out of the mouth of the most High”. So you all see why Christ is called the Word of God. Whatever the Lord says, Christ does it. He is that wisdom; he’s literally the Word of God. As God speaks, things get done, because he is the Word of God. It’s like when you watch a movie and the king says, that’s my hand: the hand is the person that does everything the king says to do. The Word of God is Christ: anything God wants done, anything that comes out of God’s mouth, the Word of God gets it done.

“And covered the earth as a cloud. I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar. I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep. In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I got a possession. With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?”

“So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest”: that’s some heavy stuff right there. “And said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thine inheritance in Israel.”

“He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.” All of this is talking about the Word of God, Christ, that eternal spirit. He will never fail; he’s going to do what the Lord says.

“In the holy tabernacle I served before him”: the holy tabernacle is where the Father dwells. The Word of God was there with the Father, serving before him. “And so was I established in Sion. Likewise in the beloved city he gave me rest, and in Jerusalem was my power.”

“By the word of the Lord were the heavens made”: the Word of God created the heavens. “And all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.” That’s some heavy stuff right there, more than we’ll go into now.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word was one of them powers in the beginning. When it says the Word was God, it literally means that in the beginning that wisdom, the Word of God, was a power there with his father.

“The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him”: by whom? By the Word of God. Who is the Word of God? Christ. He made all things. If all things were created by him, that makes him a God. Not just that: that makes him our God. If he created us, he’s our God, and the Old Testament shows it.

sense.text: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” The beginning of what? The beginning of creation. A lot of times when we read this, we go into how the Most High created the earth and the things on the earth. But the Most High has got to send his Holy Spirit for you to understand it: he gives us a little glimpse into things that were created in the heavens. When you hear heavens, you all think it’s just talking about the moon and the stars.

“And the earth was without form and void”: there was nothing here. It was a void; it had no form. “And darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.” What is the waters that he’s moving upon the face of? Space.

“And God said, Let there be light”: that’s how you know he was dealing with space. “And there was light.” Remember, wisdom was the first thing created in creation, so this is telling you when wisdom, the Word of God, was created.

Genesis is the beginning of creation, and it’s not just talking about when the earth was created. Genesis is also going into when Christ and the angels were created. It doesn’t go too much into how they were created; it gives you little hints and dark parables. The Lord told Moses don’t make that known unto them; make it in a parable, so the wise may understand.

So when it says let there be light, it’s talking about Christ. That’s the first thing God created: he created Christ, the Word of God, which is that light. Some people might say, what are you talking about, Deacon, that light is not Christ. Christ is the first of all things created by the Father.

“And God saw the light, that it was good”. We know this is not the sun, the moon, the stars or none of that. That light he created in the beginning is talking about Christ, because we know that Christ is the first thing created, and this is the first day.

precepts.why:
“Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” The work is the creation of the earth and everything. In order for God’s work to appear, he caused that light to come forth, letting you know it’s that light that created everything.

“Upon the second day thou madest the spirit of the firmament”: that’s when he created the heavens.

Start at verse one again to explain that light. “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God”: he was with his father. “And the Word was God”: that Word is an eternal power, just like the Father. “The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him”, by that Word, by that light, “and without him was not any thing made that was made.”

“In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness”: that goes back to the Lord bringing forth that light so that his work might appear. “And the darkness comprehended it not.” That even goes into when he came on this earth: there was darkness on this earth, and he was that light, but nobody understood. He created everything; he is a God. When he came on the earth, the people did not understand that.

“There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”. What light? The same light in Genesis, the Word of God, the Son of God: that’s who that light is. “That all men through him might believe. He was not that Light”: John was not that light, “but was sent to bear witness of that Light.”

“That was the true Light”: the Word of God is the true light, “which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.” He created everybody that comes into this world. He’s the man, but God created him: his father created him, and he created all of us.

Read verse three again: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by the Word of God, the light of God. So his father did not create us: his father said the word, and he created us.

sense.text:
Back to the beginning after John 1: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” The God that created the heaven and the earth is the Word of God, the light of God. All things were made by him, so the Father did not create us with his own hands: the Father said the word, and the Son created us.

And the earth was made of matter. God took matter, elements, and manipulated them to put the earth together, the same way he later took the dust of the ground and made man.
“The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters”: the waters there are space. The Spirit of God moved upon space.

“And God said, Let there be light”: here Christ was created, in a celestial form. Let there be light, and the Son, the Word of God, was created.

The first day, the second day, the third day are not twenty-four hours. Moses had it written that way so that we in this earthly form could understand what was done. Christ was there with the Lord from the beginning, before the earth was ever created. The Most High God is called Ancient because he was before days; with him time does not exist. The sun and the moon were made to tell time on the earth, so on the first day and the second day there were really no days. The first day is the first thing God did, the first thing that came out of his mouth that he told Christ to do; the second thing he called the second day, the third thing the third day, and on to the fifth.

precepts.why:
This explains how it took place in the time of creation: “For as soon as thy word went forth the work was made.” The Word of God is Christ. As soon as the Lord said, let there be fishes and so forth, Christ went forth, the Word, which is a God which could create, and boom, it was done. The work was made immediately. There were no twenty-four hours.

“For immediately there was great and innumerable fruit”: when the Lord created trees, the fruits were innumerable, popping out at once. So the first day, the second day, the third day, the fourth day are only the first, second, third and fourth thing that came out of the Lord’s mouth for Christ to do.

In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and Solomon says what he made it of: “For thy Almighty hand, that made the world of matter.” The world was made of matter.

In science matter is anything that takes up space and has mass, meaning it has volume and can be weighed; any substance that exists and can be physically touched. It is composed of atoms, too small to see with your eyes, and exists as solid, liquid or gas. A rock, water and the human body are all matter. Matter is broken down into pure substances and mixtures, and the pure substances are the elements and compounds. God created the earth from matter, and God created man from matter.

“For this man, that of earthly matter maketh brittle vessels”: man was also made of matter. So the earth is made of matter and man is made of matter.

Read it again: man came from earthly matter, and that earthly matter is the elements. God manipulated the earth and the water and the elements, and that is how man was created. All of that you find in a man. That is why the human body is made up of so much water, something like eighty percent.

Solomon is speaking: “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are”, meaning the things that were created. Solomon understood them because he created them: he was Christ, that eternal spirit. “Namely, to know how the world was made”: that is why he could say in Wisdom of Solomon 15:13 that man was created of matter, and in 11:17 that the world was made of matter.

“And the operation of the elements”: the world was made by the operating, changing and mixing of elements. When God created the heaven and the earth, it was elements put together to create the earth; the Most High God manipulated elements, and Solomon understood that. Man was created from the dust of the earth, and that dust is the element of the earth. God manipulated earth, water, all them elements, formed atoms, and atoms make cells, and he made a body. That is how the Lord creates things into existence.

Matter creates humans by forming the building blocks of our bodies, atoms, elements like carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen coming together in complex arrangements. That is what God did when he created Adam: he brought the elements together, forming, manipulating and mixing them, and created man from nothing. Look in the human body and you find the same things you find in the earth: copper, iron, zinc. Your body needs iron, a little copper and zinc to be healthy, the same things that are in the earth. The plants take them from the earth, and when we eat the food it nourishes this body we are in, which is earth.

The periodic table is incomplete. It is the limited knowledge Satan gave to Edom to understand; Solomon understood the entire table, far beyond this. He manipulated elements you cannot even see to create things; mix hydrogen and oxygen and it creates water.

Solomon was given an understanding of the elements, way more than is in that incomplete table. The table is not complete for Edom because Edom’s purpose for the elements is to destroy and defile; Solomon was given that wisdom to fix, to heal and to help, so for him it was complete.

“The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt”: all of matter, and all part of the body. Water is in the body; fire is in the body too, it is called heat; iron is in the body; and taste your tears when you cry and there is salt. “Flour of wheat, honey, milk”: milk is in the body as well. “And the blood of the grape”, wine, which is good for the body, “and oil, and clothing.”

“All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.” When a sinner gets hold of them, Edom makes them bad for you. You can have flour, but he bleaches it and you get the white one. White rice is bad, white flour is bad, white sugar is bad; flip it, and brown sugar, brown wheat, brown rice and black rice are good. Esau just takes things, turns them around and makes them evil.

“For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the spirit, and the water, and the blood.” The spirit is the spirit of man that the Lord put in that body. It says water because water is matter, part of the elements. And the blood: the iron and all these things we have been reading about are found in your blood. Any time the doctor wants to know if something is wrong with you he takes your blood work, because that is where he finds the iron and the rest.

They bear witness in earth because that is what your body is made of.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”: the Most High using and manipulating elements to create man, the dirt, the tin, all the elements that are there. And he created us perfect, from the building block, the atom, all the way into the cells.

Esau got hold of this with what they call stem cell research. They found some of our immortal genes in a sister and started doing research, and through stem cells they clone food and animals, and they are trying to clone humans, and probably already did, and that thing is a demon. Esau goes deep down inside the cell, the simplest makeup of a human being, trying to be like God. Even trees are created from matter, from elements, and he goes into the genetic makeup of the seed to remove the seed or make the fruit sweeter or bigger. Every living thing has DNA, the code of a human being; plants have DNA too, and Esau manipulates the DNA of the plants, splices the tomato into the grape to make it bigger. He is a Frankenstein.

If man has a code that creates him, man has a designer, just as a person who creates code in technology is called a designer. That means there is a God. Esau understands this. The Bible proves it first and foremost, and his science gives further conclusion that there is a God, until World War II, when they dropped that bomb and said no more God, now we are God, worship us. The bomb is made the same way God created the sun: the atomic bomb is them splitting atoms and mixing elements. When God said let there be two lights in the sky, he manipulated and mixed elements to create the moon and the sun, the same way the white man manipulates and mixes elements to create that nuclear bomb on the earth, which is like a sun.

One instance that took place: “Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.” When Aaron did this the Lord was manipulating the dust, creating stuff out of elements, and the dust became living lice. “It became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.”

“And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not.” They tried to do the same thing and could not bring forth lice like the Lord did. The white man tries to mimic everything God does; he has Satan working with him, and with his science he is literally trying to be like God.

The human body is oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, zinc, iron, iodine, magnesium, sodium, chlorine, sulfur, potassium, phosphorus, calcium: all elements, all literally found in the earth of the ground. The same things that are in the earth are in our body, and we need them for our body to be healthy; the food we eat comes from the earth that has these things in it. This goes with Wisdom of Solomon 7: God understood the world was made by elements.
