sense.text: “Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth”: God manipulated water to create birds and fishes. Water is an element, and that is where they came from. Birds and fishes came from water because the Lord manipulated elements and created them out of elements, and put code, DNA, in them. Christ did this; he is the one who created all these things.
“And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth”, “and God saw that it was good.” The one creating all these things is the Word of God.

“Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth”: the beasts of the earth were created from the earth, as the fishes and the birds were created from water. God manipulated the earth and created these animals, and the next verses show who else came from the earth.

“Let us make man in our image”: man was created like the beasts, from the earth. The same way the cattle were created from the earth, he created man from the earth; we did not come from the waters. “Let us” lets you know there were powers there in the beginning. “After our likeness.”

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him”: the man created in God’s own image is Adam. What we are reading here is Genesis 2; this is an abbreviation of it. “Male and female created he them”: that is Genesis 2.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply”: this is Genesis 3 and 4, when this took place. “And replenish the earth”: that is Genesis 4 and 5. Everything read in here is an abbreviation.

“Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed”, “to you it shall be for meat.” When God created us from the earth he gave us the fruits and the herbs to eat. When we eat them they nourish this body, which is from the earth. The fruits get their vitamins and minerals from the earth, we eat the food, and it goes into our body.

“And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made”: the God here that ended his work is the Word of God. He finished creating.

“And he rested on the seventh day”: God resting on the seventh day means he went into Paradise. It is talking about a place.

precepts.why:
“O Lord, who bearest rule, thou spakest at the beginning, when thou didst plant the earth”, when God created the earth, “and that thyself alone, and commandedst the people, And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life”. He breathed into Adam the breath of life: that eternal spirit, his Son. He created him in the flesh, “and he was made living before thee.”

“And thou leadest him into paradise”: after he was created, God led him into Paradise. So when it says God rested on the seventh day, it means he went into Paradise.

The body he formed is the elements: he was manipulating the earth and so forth to form Adam, and after he formed that body he put that eternal spirit into it. The Father did that.

“I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.” He came out through the mouth: the Lord breathed, the Father put him in that body, breathed into him the breath of life. That is him coming out, the eternal spirit.

This explains what it means that God rested on the sabbath day. “For we which have believed do enter into rest”: those of us that believe do enter into rest. “As he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.” The works were already finished, so what is he talking about? “For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day”: the seventh day is talking about a place.

We read that in 2 Esdras. The seventh day sabbath is talking about Paradise. When it says God rested on the sabbath day, he went into Paradise after he created the earth, and from Paradise he started ruling the heaven and the earth.

sense.text:
“Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.” This is showing the creation in Genesis: the heaven creation and also the creation on earth, and the completion of it. When it said in the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, it is talking about the creation of the heavenly realm and the creation of the earthly realm.

When it says the heavens, you all are thinking it was just the sky and the stars and the moon. No, it is talking about galaxies. Remember, Genesis is the beginning, and Genesis goes into everything that was created: Adam, and even when the angels, righteous and good and evil were created, if you are spiritual and you can see it.

So what is “all the host of them”? The host is the angels, Satan, men, birds, planets, stars, galaxies: everything that is in the heaven and in the earth was created. That is what Moses is letting us know. He gave us the breakdown of everything that God created; he gave us our abbreviation.

“Who is the image of the invisible God”: Christ is the image of the invisible God. The Father is called the invisible God because no one ever saw him. The word of God, his Son Christ, is the only one that ever saw him; that is why he is called the invisible God. It doesn’t mean he has an invisible body. He is the image, meaning Christ looks like him.

“The firstborn of every creature”: Christ was the first thing created, the first thing in day one. A lot of things were created on that day one, things on a celestial level: Satan, good, evil, the angels. Everything that was in the heavens was created on day one. That is why it says all the host in heaven was created and all the host on earth was created.

“For by him were all things created”: the him there is Christ. Christ created the angels, and guess who he also created: Satan. By him were all things created, meaning Satan was created by him and the angels were created by Christ.

The things “that are in heaven, and that are in earth” were created by Christ, by the word of God. That is why brothers don’t fully understand the eternity and the power of the one who came and died for us. He created everything; he is a God.

“Visible and invisible”: the things you can see were created by him, and the things you cannot see were created by him, “whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.” All things were created by the word of God, and all things were created for him: the Father said, create them things, and they are for you.
“And he is before all things”: Christ was the first thing created. That is what it is saying.

precepts.why:
Christ created Satan, and here Satan is tempting him: “If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.” This is what Jesus answered Satan while he was tempting him: “Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.”

What is Christ doing here? He is telling Satan, I’m your God. The one who made all things, Satan included, is the one Satan is asking to worship him.

The point is in verse 12, read from verse 9. Satan “brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God”. Who is the Son of God? Christ is the Son of God, and he knows he is. The Son of God is also the word of God, and he created everything: all things were created by him and for him.

Satan says “cast thyself down from hence: For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.”

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” What is he telling Satan? Don’t tempt me. The Lord thy God that Satan was tempting is Christ, the one that created him.

“By the word of the Lord were the heavens made”: by the word of the Lord, which is Christ, were the heavens made, “and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.” The same way the Lord breathed breath into things, Christ breathed breath into things too.

sense.text: “Thou shalt be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder”: we shall be visited by the Lord of hosts with thunder, “and with earthquake, and great noise”. So who is the Lord of hosts? That’s Christ.

precepts.why:
“As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.”

The Lord of hosts goes into Lord of armies: host means armies. But the host also goes into everything that was created. So we know the Lord of hosts there is talking about Christ. He defends Jerusalem, he delivers it, and passing over he preserves it: he is our Passover.

sense.text: Back to it: “Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.” All the host of the heaven and the earth was finished, meaning the angels, everything, was finished in the beginning. So when it says the Lord of hosts, it means he created everything. But the Lord of hosts is also going into the armies of Israel, the armies in heaven and earth.

precepts.why: “And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.” All the host of the Lord went out of the land of Egypt. Who is the host of the Lord that went out from the land of Egypt? The next scripture shows it: the armies of Israel.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt”. Mine armies and my people, the children of Israel: the armies of Israel, that’s the host of the Lord.

“Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts”. Who was there with King David? Who is the Lord of hosts? That’s Christ. David says, I come before you in the name of the Lord of hosts, meaning the lord of the armies in heaven and earth.

“The God of the armies of Israel”: the Lord of hosts is the God of the armies of Israel. It is all talking about the word of God; it is all talking about Christ that created everything.

“And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The Lord of hosts is the God over Israel”. The Lord of hosts is the God over Israel, the God over the twelve tribes of Israel, and the Lord of hosts is Christ. That’s not hard to understand.

This is what Bishop means when he says the God we were dealing with right through the Old Testament is Christ. People argue that the capital LORD is the Father. We were taught this when we were younger: when you see the capital L, that’s the Father, and the lowercase L, that’s the Son. But as we grow in this truth we understand it is interchangeable. Sometimes it is the Lord speaking, sometimes it is the angel speaking on his behalf, sometimes it is the Son speaking, or the Son speaking on the behalf of his Father.
“Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory.” He is our King, brothers: the Lord of hosts, which is the word of God, Christ.

“The Lord is my strength and song”, “he is my God”: the Lord is our God. “I will prepare him an habitation; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.”

“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” Who is the Lord here that is a man of war? Who is the Lord that has been warring with us in the Bible, warring with the nations on our behalf? It is talking about Christ.

Here is the proof that the Lord who wars for us is Christ. “The Lord hath prepared his throne in the heavens”: the Lord has his throne in the heaven, and the Lord this is talking about is Christ, “and his kingdom ruleth over all.”

“Bless the Lord, ye his angels”: who created the angels? Christ created the angels; all things were created by him and for him. Bless the Lord, ye his angels “that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” Bless ye the Lord, all ye host, “ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.”

“Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion”. The Lord here is the Lord of hosts, our King. It is talking about the word of God, Christ: that’s who we are reading about right here.

“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.” The Lord of hosts goes forth and fights against those nations, as he fought in the day of battle. So when was the Lord fighting for us in the day of battle?

sense.text: “The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.”

“The first man is of the earth, earthy”: the first man Adam came from the earth. “The second man is the Lord from heaven.” You see who Christ is: he’s the Lord, and he’s from heaven. He is that eternal spirit, he is the Son of God; he created all things. He’s the Lord from heaven.

“While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.” Though he had done so many miracles before them, they did not believe Christ.
Pay attention to what he is saying: “Lord, who hath believed our report?” They don’t want to believe us. “And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

“Therefore they could not believe”, because of what Isaiah said again: “He hath blinded their eyes”, and hardened their hearts, “that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” This is what the Lord did: he blinded our people’s eyes and their hearts, so that they can’t see and understand. The I that should heal them is Christ.

“These things said” Isaiah, “when he saw his glory, and spake of him.” He saw Christ’s glory, and he spoke of Christ. These scriptures, brothers, are on another level. Isaiah saw Christ and saw his glory; he saw the Lord from heaven. They keep playing with us like we don’t know what we are talking about, but right through the Bible it is Christ; right through the Bible it is him.

This is Christ’s glory and what Isaiah saw. “In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord”: the Lord here is the same Lord in Corinthians, the second Adam, the Lord from heaven, the Lord come down from heaven. Isaiah saw Christ. He saw the word of God, the Lord the God of Israel, the one that created the heavens and the earth and that created Israel, “sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” This is the Lord Isaiah saw.
“Each one had six wings”: these are the angels that are around Christ, “with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.”
“Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.” Who is the Lord of hosts? Christ.

“Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips”. This is how Isaiah felt when he saw the Lord: he saw Christ in his glory, sitting on his throne in heaven, because that’s where he is. He dwelt “in the midst of a people of unclean lips”, and his eyes saw “the King, the Lord of hosts”: he saw our King, Christ, and he knew who he was. He knew the Lord of hosts.

One flew to him with a live coal “taken with the tongs from off the altar: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.” Your sins are taken away. The Lord can take away your sins just like that. Brothers, understand that once you are one of the elect, and you are trying hard and you are sincere in this walk, the Lord is going to show you mercy.

“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go for us? That is the same as let us create man in our image: that is the powers in the heaven. Guess what: Christ’s Father is not there. It is Christ and the angels. “Then said I, Here am I; send me.”

What does God tell Isaiah to do? “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” You hear it and you don’t understand; you see, but you don’t perceive. “Make the heart of this people fat”, and “shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes”, “and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed”: healed by the Lord.

precepts.why:
Back to John to weigh it again: “That the saying of” Isaiah “the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?” “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” The I that should heal them is the Lord, Christ. That’s what Isaiah saw.

“These things said” Isaiah “when he saw his glory, and spake of him”: he spoke of Christ. That is who Isaiah was speaking about in Isaiah 6. He saw the Lord of hosts, he saw the King, and that was Christ: he saw him in his eternal form in the heavens. Remember Corinthians 15: the last Adam is the Lord from heaven.

When the spirit opened this up, it was plain: the Lord we read about right through the scripture is Christ on the throne. It is not until the end that we see the Father, in Daniel 7. That’s Christ’s Father.

sense.text: “And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. Who is speaking here? This is all the Lord speaking. Why does it say we are his firstborn? Were we the first nation created? No. So when he says we are the firstborn, what is he talking about? We are the first he created.

precepts.why:
“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” The world was not yet made, meaning the earth was not made as yet.

This is telling you that on the first day we were there: Christ created us. He created things up there on the first day. That is why Genesis 2:1 says all the host of heaven was created, meaning we were there with him before the earth was created. Israel is his son, his firstborn, meaning we are the first he created.

“But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn”: we are the firstborn. “Thy only begotten”: we are his only begotten, the same way Christ is the Father’s only begotten. He created everything, but we were created in his image and his likeness. We were created to be his sons, and we were the first created. “And thy fervent lover, are given into their hands.”

“If the world now be made for our sakes”: in Genesis it says God created man in his image, and Adam brought forth sons in his image after his likeness, and he told us to subdue, and to subdue is to rule. The earth was created for the sons of God. But we wanted to be like the nations, so the Most High said, you are going to die like men; I’m taking your power away from you. You want to mess with the she devil.

“And thou shalt say unto him, The Lord God of the Hebrews hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou wouldest not hear.”

The Lord God of the Hebrews is all talking about Christ. When Christ said Israel is my son, my firstborn, it is all talking about our God, the Lord of hosts: the entity that created us, the power that created the planet earth and the universe, under orders from his Father that created him.

sense.text:
The one that was talking to Moses, that was in the wilderness with us, was Christ. It was always him right through the Bible. We never heard the Father’s voice; we never saw the Father.

“All our fathers were under the cloud”: the cloud is the chariot, what they call UFOs, “and all passed through the sea”.
“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: it says in the cloud because Moses went up there in the cloud, by the chariot, and got the laws and came and taught them to us.

“And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” That cloud that followed them, that rock that followed us, that was with us when we were in the wilderness with Moses, that was Christ. It was the Lord of hosts.

precepts.why:
“When Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war”: the Philistines were going to come to war against us if the Lord led us through the land of the Philistines, “and they return to Egypt”.

“But God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea”: the Lord led us through the wilderness of the Red sea. “And the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt. And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him”, for Joseph had made them swear: “God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.”

“And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light”. That Lord that went before us is Christ: the same rock that followed us, and that rock was Christ. “He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.”

sense.text:
It was always Christ, brothers and sisters. It was always the word of God, always him: that’s who we dealt with right through.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn”: this is what happened in Egypt when we came out of Egypt, when God was destroying all the firstborns in Egypt. Now who is the God that was doing this? Keep reading. “They acknowledged this people to be the sons of God”: they acknowledged, these people are the sons of God.
“For while all things were in quiet silence”: while everybody was sleeping, sleeping on the Passover in the night, “and that night was in the midst of her swift course”.

“Thine Almighty word”: the Almighty word is the word of God; this is talking about the Lord. While the Egyptians were sleeping, the Almighty word leaped down “from heaven out of thy royal throne”: the royal throne that Isaiah saw him in. He came out of that throne. He leaped out of that throne saying, I’m about to get dirty right now, I’m about to get bloody right now, “as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”. He destroyed things when he came; when he jumped down he started killing them Egyptians.

He brought the commandment “as a sharp sword”, and standing up he filled all things with death: he killed all the firstborn in Egypt with death. Who did that? The Almighty word, the Lord, leaping off from his throne.

“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations”: this is in the last days. Our Lord is going to come forth and fight against Amalek, fight against Europe, fight against the Arabs.

“As when he fought in the day of battle”: when he fought for us, when he delivered us out of Egypt. There’s a book called the wars of the Lord, and they think they could hide it from us, but when you read the scriptures you can put it all together and read about it.

The Lord was always there fighting with us. The Lord told Gideon, when you hear me running on the trees, just know that’s me. David told that boy he was going to kill him with this stone: it’s not just me, the Lord of hosts is fighting with me. That’s why David says the Lord taught my hands to war; the Lord was there with David, fighting with him and protecting him. There are some things you all don’t fully understand and see yet, but you are going to understand soon.

“And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east”: Christ’s feet are going to stand on the Mount of Olives when he touches down in the last days.

“And the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west.” That is where he is coming back: the same place Christ left from, the Mount of Olives. When he comes back, that’s where he is going to start popping off at, right there.
“And he brought out of him a merciful man”: that merciful man is Moses, “which found favour in the sight of all flesh, even Moses, beloved of God”. He was beloved of God, and his memorial is blessed.
“He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.” Pay attention to how high the Lord lifted Moses up.

“By his words he caused the wonders to cease”: by his word, by God’s word. “And he made him glorious in the sight of kings”: he made Moses glorious in the sight of kings. “And gave him a commandment for his people”: he gave Moses the commandments to teach us.

“And shewed him part of his glory.” Who showed Moses part of his glory? Christ is the one, his word: that is who showed Moses part of his glory. People say, see, that was God’s glory, Moses saw God the Father, Christ’s father’s glory. It was not.

“He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud”. The dark cloud is the Chariot. So Moses went into the Chariot and sat with Christ, and Christ taught Moses and showed Moses a lot of things.

Remember what it says: he made him to hear his voice. There is a scripture that says no man ever heard the voice of the Father, so we know this is Christ.

precepts.why:
“For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness”: the light that shined out of darkness is Christ. God commanded Christ to shine out of darkness, meaning he created Christ.

That light “hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.” In the face of Jesus Christ you can see the glory of God. What Moses and all of us were seeing, that shine Moses was seeing when he saw Christ: that glory is the glory of God.

Read on: “But we have this treasure”. Esdras also talks about that treasure: that light is that treasure. So the glory of God that Moses saw is the light that shines and emanates from Christ. That is the part of his glory Moses was shown.

Christ is the one “Who is the image of the invisible God”. Christ is the image of his Father, so if you see Christ’s glory, whose glory is he? In Revelation it tells you both of them is a light. If you see the glory of Christ you see the glory of the Father.

That is why the glory Moses saw was Christ’s, and still it is called the glory of God: because the Father is invisible, nobody has ever seen him, and Christ is his image.

Christ made it clear for anybody that has questions: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time”. Nobody ever heard the voice of Christ’s Father, at any time. No matter if you are going to read something about thus saith the Lord, the Lord God the Almighty: it is not him, not Christ’s Father. Christ knows, so he is letting us know. It’s simple like that.

“Nor seen his shape.” He had to put emphasis on the shape, because they are saying the shape Moses saw in the wilderness is the Father. No: I showed Moses the glory of me, and I am the image of the invisible God. The invisible God means nobody ever saw him; that is why he is called an invisible God.

“And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not. Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” Everything you read about, Christ is saying that is me. The voice you heard, that was me; the back you saw, that was me; the scriptures testify of me. Thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, the Lord of hosts: a lot of you thought Isaiah 6 was the Father. No, that’s the Lord, that’s Christ.

“And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.” “But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you.” “I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only?”

“Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.” Moses is the one accusing you; Christ doesn’t have to. That is why he said nobody ever heard the voice and nobody ever saw the shape: he understood they trusted in Moses and the law, and the law says Moses heard the voice of God and saw part of God’s glory. Christ is fixing all of that now: that was never the Father. Nobody ever heard his voice, nobody ever saw his shape.

“For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” It was all Christ Moses was writing about: Israel is my son, even my firstborn. Moses understood it was always Christ. Exodus, Genesis, Deuteronomy, Numbers, Leviticus, the Lord of hosts: that was me Moses was writing about. “But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?”

sense.text: “If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.” “Then said the Jews unto him, Now we know that thou hast a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets”. Abraham and the prophets died, yet you are saying if a man keeps your sayings he will never taste death? “Art thou greater than our father Abraham, which is dead?”

“Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.” That’s some heavy stuff right there. And he saw it: Abraham was around. The Lord that came to Abraham in Genesis and talked to him, that was the Lord.
“Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?” You ain’t even fifty years old, how the hell you see Abraham?

“Before Abraham was, I am.” Why did they want to kill him when he said that? He was saying that he is the I am. Get the big stone, kill him: they got angry because he called himself the I am, and it was time for him to get out of there. “Then took they up stones to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple”.

And he is the I am. He created us. He is the one that was in the wilderness with Moses; he is the one that told Moses, I am sent you. And what is so heavy: Abraham is his son. Before Abraham was, I am: I existed long before Abraham, I was there in creation, I created everything. He is saying I am the God of this world.

“Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. What is the sign? “Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.” His name is going to be called Emmanuel.

What does Emmanuel mean? God with us. It literally means our God is born in flesh and is on the earth with us. That is what that babe means: that child is our God being born on the earth.
“Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good.” He is going to be known to refuse evil and choose good. He shall come into a body, a body undefiled.

precepts.why:
“For she knoweth and understandeth all things”: she knows and understands all things, we don’t. “And she shall lead me soberly in my doings, and preserve me in her power. So shall my works be acceptable, and then shall I judge thy people righteously”.

Who is speaking here? King Solomon. King Solomon knew who he was; the Lord gave him a level of understanding. “And be worthy to sit in my father’s seat.” Christ is sitting right now on the right hand of God: that is the Father’s seat.

“For I was a witty child, and had a good spirit. Yea rather, being good, I came into a body undefiled.” By being good he came into a body undefiled. Solomon is prophesying about himself, being good, coming back on this earth and being born as Christ.

That is the child of Isaiah 7 that knows to refuse the evil and choose the good: he shall come into a body, a body undefiled.

“Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.”

When it says God is with us, it literally means our God is born in flesh and is on the earth with us. That is what Emmanuel means. That child is our God being born on the earth.

The Most High is playing no games; we are making it clear today. “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him”: nobody can compare to our God.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

“Afterward”: after he gave us the laws and all of that, “did he shew himself upon earth”. Did he do what? Show himself, upon the earth. Our God came and showed himself upon the earth: that is the sign of Isaiah 7, God with us.

“And the Word was made flesh”: the Word, which is our God, was made flesh, “and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.” He was the only begotten of the Father.

The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us: that is our God dwelling amongst us. That Word that created all of us, that’s our God. That is Emmanuel, God with us.

sense.text:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”. That child, that son, is given unto us. “And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: he is the ruler, he’s the king.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God”. Right through the Bible you read about the Mighty God: that’s talking about Christ. God Almighty, that’s Christ. “The everlasting Father”: when you read the Bible and it talks about the everlasting Father, a lot of times it’s talking about Christ; sometimes it’s talking about his Father. “The Prince of Peace”: he’s the Prince of Peace.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end”. There shall be no end to his government and his peace.

So that son that is given unto us, that son that is born, is our God. That’s why it says thou shalt call his name Emmanuel: our God is with us, dwelling with us. He came in the flesh, walking with us.

precepts.why:
“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.”

Christ referred to himself as the Almighty. He says I’m the Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, which is to come, the Almighty. So the Almighty God you read about in the Old Testament is also talking about Christ: he is The mighty God of Isaiah 9.

“For the kingdom is the Lord’s: and he is the governor among the nations.” That is the same thing we just read: “and the government shall be upon his shoulder”. The kingdom is the Lord’s; it’s talking about Christ, and he is the governor among the nations.

sense.text:
“No man hath seen God at any time”: no man has ever seen God at any time. “The only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father”: the only one that was in the bosom of the Father is Christ, and Christ is the only begotten Son. “He hath declared him.”

You all try to say Christ’s God is our God. No: God created Christ, and Christ created us. We’ve been dealing with Christ all the time. Christ came and died, and now our adoption is about to take place: we are about to see our grandfather, Christ’s Father. Then he becomes Our Father which art in heaven. He’s our Father, but we’ve got to be adopted for it to be Our Father. Just think about the power of Christ, then what about the grandfather: there’s infinite power.

Asked who he was, John confessed he was not the Christ. “He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias.” Go to Isaiah and see the exact words of what Isaiah said.

precepts.why:
“Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the Lord’s hand double for all her sins.”

“The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.” For our what? Our God. John was preparing the way of the Lord, so Christ is our God. Isaiah called the Lord our God. Is that hard? Is it rocket science? Am I crazy? You leaders who say we are crazy for saying Christ is our God, y’all bugging.

We are not saying Christ, the Father and the Holy Spirit is one, like these Christians. We are saying Christ is the God that created us, and Christ has a God over him. And we are also the sons of God: the scripture says we are going to be gods just like him. He said the things I do you are going to do, and greater; we are going to be as he is. So we are going to be gods also, on different levels.

“And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you. Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.”

“And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.” And my what? My God. You all see that: Thomas said my Lord and my God. You can’t go around that. Everybody is not going to get it; these things are spiritually discerned.

sense.text: “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God”. Christ was in the form of God, because he was made in the image of his God. “Thought it not robbery to be equal with God”: when it says he thought it not robbery to be equal with God, he is the Son of God.

“But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: meaning he came in the flesh. “And was made in the likeness of men”: he came as a man. That goes back to John 1:14, the Word was made flesh.

“And being found in fashion as a man”. Who did that? Our God, Christ, the Word of God, the only begotten Son of the Father. “He humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.”
“Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him”: the Most High God has highly exalted him, “and given him a name which is above every name.” He has got a name that is above every name.

precepts.why:
“And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day. But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.”

So when it says he was equal with God, it is when he said he is the Son of God. To say you are the Son of God is making yourself equal to God. They wanted to kill him because he said he is the Son of God, that spiritual celestial being. That is Philippians 2: he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, because he is the Son of God.

“Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.” What he sees the Father do, the Son does likewise. Even in creation: the reason he was able to create is his Father taught him all these things. I can do nothing unless the Father teaches me or shows me.

Read it again: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,)”. Christ is the only begotten of the Father.

The only begotten of the Father means he is the only one the Father created. Everybody is running wrong talking about God. God gave the Word; Christ is the one that created us. Christ is the only one that was created by the Father, and he was the firstborn of all creation. The Father created him, he created us, and the Father taught him how to create.

“He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?”

God gave up his only Son for us, brothers and sisters. His only Son he gave up for us, so he is going to freely give us all things.

“How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit”: that Spirit that was in that flesh, that spirit in that body, is called Christ. Christ is that eternal Spirit.

“Offered himself without spot to God”: he offered himself without spot, without sin, unto God, to “purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God”. So now we are able to serve God.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”.

sense.text:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son”: meaning the only Son that he created, the only Son that came from him. That’s what only begotten means. Before Christ adopted us, we are not the sons of God; we were his sons in the beginning, under Christ.

“That whosoever believeth in him”: whosoever believeth in his Son, that eternal Spirit, that God, “should not perish, but have everlasting life.”

precepts.why:
This explains John 3:16 plainly. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

The high priest that same year said unto them, “Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The world is the nation of Israel: that the whole nation of Israel perish not.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation”. To die for who? That nation. That’s the world: that nation is talking about the nation of Israel. That explains John 3:16, for God so loved the world. See how easy that is.

“The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record. For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.”

The world that went after Christ is Israel. There are many other scriptures that explain that, but these two scriptures go right to the point: the world God so loved is the nation of Israel.

sense.text:
After showing that the world that went after Christ is Israel, the class goes to how Israel becomes the sons of God. “But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God”: as many as received Christ, Christ gave them power to become the sons of God. Now we have become the sons of God. Before that we were Christ’s sons; right through the Old Testament it was Christ we were dealing with.

“Even to them that believe on his name”: even unto them that believe on Christ’s name.
“Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.” This sonship is not of blood or of the will of man; it is of God.

precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us”: of God’s own will he begat us. All the time we were reading about the begotten of the Father, and Christ is the only begotten Son; we kept reading that. Now the scripture is saying that the Father has begotten us. Christ is not the only begotten no more.

He begat us “with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We are not perfect like Christ, but we are a kind of firstfruits.

“I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” You can’t go to the Father except you go through Christ. Receiving Christ is the only way to that power to become the sons of God.

“He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.”

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” The life is in the Son, so it is them that believe on his name who receive it.

“For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.” Through Christ we got access by one Spirit unto the Father. Before, we had no access; now through Christ we got access to the Father.

“Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”: we are of the household of God. We “are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: Christ himself is the cornerstone.

sense.text: “Ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.” We have received the spirit of adoption.

“The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.” We are adopted, and we became joint-heirs with Christ: joint-heirs to the Father with Christ.

People think the adoption was us being adopted to Christ. No: we are adopted to the Father. Christ was the God we were dealing with right through; now we are able to see our grandfather. Christ has got to clean us up and purify us first before he takes us to his Father: you all too dirty, I got to clean you all up before I take you all to my Father. And not all of you are going to be taken.

“If so be that we suffer with him”: if you suffer with Christ, the same suffering Christ went through, if you go through it, then you are going to be joint-heirs.

precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ”: God predestinated us to be adopted as his children by Jesus Christ. That adoption was predestined.

“To himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”: it is according to the Father’s will.

sense.text:
“Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.” They heard a voice coming from heaven. A lot of times people read this and answer that it was God speaking. No: nobody ever heard God’s voice.

Do you understand what a messenger is? The word angel means messenger. Angels speak on the behalf of God.

“Others said, An angel spake to him.” The angel is speaking, but the angel is speaking on the behalf of the Father: I have glorified it, and will keep glorifying it. No one has ever heard the voice of the Father; it was always Christ, or an angel speaking on the behalf of the Father.

precepts.why:
“The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him”: God gave the revelation to Christ, “to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass.” That is why in the scriptures God showed Christ certain things, and Christ comes to us telling us thus saith the Lord.

What Christ did: “he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John.” His angel, meaning the angels belong to Christ. God showed it to Christ, Christ showed it unto the angel, and the angel showed it unto his servants. That is the divine order.

“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending.” This is the angel saying this, speaking on the behalf of Christ. When you read in Revelation, that is an angel speaking, but he is speaking on the behalf of Christ.

sense.text:
“Thus saith the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker.” Don’t let this go over your head. Who is speaking here? Christ is speaking here, on the behalf of the Father also. Christ refers to himself as the Holy One of Israel, and the Holy One of Israel has a maker. So when you hear thus saith the Lord the Holy One of Israel and his Maker, who is his maker? The Father.

“Ask me of things to come concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me.”

“I have made the earth, and created man upon it.” The Holy One of Israel and his Maker: the Father told Christ what to do and he did it. “I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens, and all their host have I commanded”: all the hosts, the angels, I commanded them. I am the Lord of hosts.
“I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways.”

precepts.why: “I am the Lord, your Holy One, the creator of Israel”: so you understand who the Holy One is, the creator of Israel. “Your King”: who is our King? Christ.

“From Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father.”

We are made kings and priests unto Christ and Christ’s Father. And Christ’s Father is now our father too.

sense.text:
“Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” That is different from the temple of Christ: Christ’s God, his temple is beyond all heavens. Not my temple, but in the temple of my God. “And he shall go no more out”: we ain’t going to go out.

“And I will write upon him the name of my God.” What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou canst tell? You don’t know his name. Christ says, right through the Bible it is me you have been dealing with; I gave you different titles, and that was all me; but if you overcome I am going to give you the name of my God. Christ says it that way because Christ is our God.

“And the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God.”

“And I will write upon him my new name.” There is a new name that nobody knew but Christ himself, and that name is above all names that have ever been in heaven and in earth.

People make stuff up and say we had a meeting and said you can’t say yahawashi. Where the hell they getting this stuff from? When we teach it on the street we use the words people could understand: they know who Christ is; if we said yahawashi nobody would understand. If you want to pray and say yahawashi, that is on you. When Christ taught us to pray to the Father, we say our Father, because he is my Father now and your Father now: we are joint-heirs. If we say our Father, he knows we are speaking to him.

precepts.why: “Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him”: God has exalted Christ, and God is going to give him a new name. That is the new name Christ says he will write upon him that overcometh.

sense.text: “And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking.”

“Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die.” They said, don’t let God speak to us, Moses; you speak to us and we are going to hear. Who was that God that was speaking to us in the wilderness?

“Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not.” He wants you to be afraid of him. The Lord came with the chariot and got everybody scared; he came to prove them: you better be scared of me, I don’t play, keep my commandments.

precepts.why:
“For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest”: that is what we just read in Exodus, the black cloud that Moses went into in the wilderness.

“And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words”: that was the voice of Christ. “Which voice they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more.” In Exodus it says that voice was the voice of God; they said, we don’t want to hear that voice no more. “For they could not endure that which was commanded”: what was commanded was the Lord, and that is what they couldn’t endure. “And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake”: Moses was frightened and quaking.

“But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.” That blood of sprinkling is Christ’s blood. Abel is the old covenant of sacrifice that Moses gave us; Christ speaketh better things than Abel.

“See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth”: Moses was speaking back there on the earth; Moses gave us the laws. “Much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven”: him that speaketh from heaven is Christ, speaking better things than Abel. It is letting you know that was Christ in the wilderness speaking.

“Whose voice then shook the earth”: Christ’s voice shook the earth back then, shook the mountain. “But now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more”: yet once more, letting you know that was him in Exodus. “I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.”

“And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken”: everything that is the kingdoms and the governments set up on this earth will be removed. “That those things which cannot be shaken may remain”: those things are those of us that keep the commandments and the faith of Christ. “Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably.”

sense.text: “Who created all things by Jesus Christ”: all things were created by Jesus Christ. God used Christ to create everything.
“That now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God.” What you are learning today is the manifold wisdom of God.

precepts.why:
“For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ”: we bow our knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

“Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named”: the families in heaven and the families in earth are named after the Lord, meaning we got his name. That name is Israel: prince, as a prince you have power with God.

sense.text: “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness.”

“Even his eternal power and Godhead”: that is the name of the topic today, the eternal power and Godhead. The power of God, the power of Christ: Christ created everything, and Christ is the one God put over everything. It is all him. Right through the Bible we are reading about the Lord of hosts, the Lord God of Israel, and that was always Christ.

Because he came and died, now we get access to his Father. Now we say our Father; now we are adopted to the Father. That is what the adoption is about: us having access to the Father.

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended.” Christ is going to destroy everything. He is going to destroy these nations: he is the one that created them, and he is the one going to destroy them.

precepts.why: “For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.” We are going to stand before the judgment seat of Christ. That is who is doing the judging on this earth. Why? Because he is the one that created us, so he is the one that says, I am going to judge you all.

sense.text: “Because they know not him that sent me”: they don’t know God.
“He that hateth me hateth my Father also.” If you hate Christ, you hate the Father.
“The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do.”

“For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.” Christ learned things from the Father; he does nothing without the Father showing him and telling him what to do.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.” The Father himself is not going to judge no man; he committed all judgment unto Christ. Christ is the one that is going to judge everybody on this earth.

“That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father”: how you honour the Father, you are going to honour the Son the same way, for he is a God just like his Father. That old saying, you just like your daddy: that is yahawashi, he is just like his daddy.

“He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him.”
“The dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God”: they are going to hear the voice of the Son of God, “and they that hear shall live.”

“For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself; And hath given him authority to execute judgment also”: Christ is given authority to execute judgment on this earth. Christ got that authority.

“Because he is the Son of man”: he is Adam; that is what it is really saying.

“The hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.”
“I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just.”

precepts.why:
The last judgment is also going to be Christ. “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away.” This great white throne is Christ. All judgment was given unto Christ: the person judging everybody is Christ. He is the God that is judging this earth.

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God”: when it says stand before God, the God there is the Son of God.

“And the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” Who is written in the book of life? Israel. This is the end of all nations.
